about: The SQL an app's server/ code and migrations may run, as both SoftN backend hosts must answer it. Each case runs on a fresh database built from `schema` (without an authorizer). `migration` cases are one migration script applied inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE; `runtime` cases are one softn.sql call (`kind` query, first or execute) inside the route's transaction (`mode` write unless read). `allow` is the contract; `result`, when present, is what the call returns. `before`, when present, is an `execute` the same request made first, on the same connection. `rust` names a case the Rust host (apps/softn-host-rust/src/bridges/sql.rs, private_backend.rs) answers differently today and why. Read by apps/softn-host-php/tests/sql-parity.test.mjs and apps/softn-host-rust/src/sql_parity_tests.rs.

migration.sql: CREATE TABLE strict_items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) STRICT; ALTER TABLE strict_items ADD COLUMN tag TEXT;
migration.rust: refused: SQLite checks a STRICT table it adds a column to with an internal quick_check, which the Rust host's migration authorizer (bridges/sql.rs authorize) refuses as a PRAGMA, so the migration fails there; the PHP host lets that one check through for a verified nullable TEXT ADD (runtime/migrations.mjs)
